turns.doctor_question: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi Dr. Smith. Um, well, my manager actually suggested I come in, because... well, things at the salon have just been really, really difficult lately. I'm a hairstylist, I've been doing it since I got my associate's, and I've always prided myself on being really efficient, you know? But recently... I don't even know how to explain it, it's just like my body isn't cooperating. 

My hands feel like they’re moving through glue at work. It's so frustrating because I'll be standing there, and even just doing the absolute basics, like sectioning a client's hair or mixing color in the back room, it takes me forever now. I used to be able to whip up a formula in seconds, but now I'm just standing there with the brush and the bowl, and my arms feel so incredibly heavy. And the worst part is that people have started noticing I’m just slower than I used to be. My regulars are looking at the clock, the other girls at the washing stations are asking if I need help, and my manager had to actually adjust my booking times because I just keep running behind. I try to speed up, I really do, but it’s like I’m physically pushing through molasses just to lift a comb, and I just keep talking to my clients to try and distract them from how slow my hands are moving, but... yeah, it's just really affecting my job and I don't know why I can't just move normally anymore.

symptom_reasoning.S028: The patient describes a significant, observable decrease in motor activity, stating her hands feel like they are 'moving through glue,' her arms feel heavy, and others have noticed she is moving much slower than usual.

turns.doctor_question: Have there ever been periods in your life where you felt the exact opposite of this—where you had an unusually high amount of energy, felt like you didn't need much sleep, or felt like your mind was racing?
turns.patient_response:
Um, no... no, definitely not. Honestly, I kind of wish I did? Because that sounds like it would be really helpful right now at the salon. But no, I've never been one of those people who can just go and go and go. Like, one of the other girls I work with, Jessica, she’s always coming in with these massive iced lattes, just buzzing around the floor, talking a mile a minute and sweeping up hair before I’ve even finished my first blowout of the morning. I've never been like that, not even close. 

Even back when I was in cosmetology school, you know, when we were pulling these crazy long hours practicing on mannequins and prepping for exams just trying to finish up our associate's degrees... I was never the one with endless energy or racing thoughts. I've always needed my sleep. Like, a solid eight or nine hours, minimum, otherwise I'm a total zombie. I've never felt like I didn't need to sleep. 

And lately, it's just... well, my brain feels like it's barely crawling, just exactly like my hands. I don't even know what racing thoughts would feel like, to be honest, because everything just feels so incredibly heavy and slow and exhausting. So, no, definitely no periods of super high energy or skipping sleep. I really, really wish I could borrow some of that energy right now, though, because this whole moving-through-molasses thing is just completely ruining my booking schedule and making me look so unprofessional to my clients, and I just... I hate feeling this sluggish all the time.

symptom_reasoning.S029: The patient describes everything feeling incredibly heavy and exhausting.
symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient states her brain feels like it is barely crawling, indicating slowed or diminished thinking.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient explicitly denies ever having periods of unusually high energy or being able to 'go and go and go'.
symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient denies ever feeling like she didn't need sleep, stating she has always needed a minimum of eight or nine hours.
symptom_reasoning.S038: The patient explicitly denies experiencing racing thoughts, stating she doesn't even know what they would feel like.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever gone through a period like this before, where you felt this same kind of heavy, sluggish exhaustion for a few weeks or longer?
turns.patient_response:
Um, well... I mean, I've been tired before, like when I was pulling all-nighters finishing up my associate's degree, but it was never, ever like this. This is... it's a whole different thing entirely. Because it's not just that my arms and legs feel heavy, like I was saying about mixing the color at work. It's... it's inside, too. It's my mood. 

Like, most days, I just wake up and before I even open my eyes, before my phone alarm even goes off for my morning shift, I just have this... this heavy, flat sadness just sitting right in the middle of my chest. It's so heavy. And it just makes me feel like... like, what is even the point? You know? I spent all that time in school, saving up for my own professional shears, trying to build my Instagram portfolio so I could get a chair at a really good salon, and I had this whole timeline for my life. I was going to build up my regular clientele, maybe rent my own studio suite by the time I'm twenty-five... but now, with this sadness just weighing me down every single morning, it feels like there is absolutely no point in trying to build the life I was planning. 

I just lie there in bed looking at the ceiling and think, why bother? Why go in and try to pretend to be bubbly and do balayage and highlights when I just feel so incredibly sad and flat inside? It's just this constant, heavy feeling, and it makes everything I used to care about feel completely useless. So... no, I've never had a period quite like this before, because it's just so much worse than just being physically exhausted. It really feels like it's taking away everything I worked for.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient describes waking up most days with a constant, 'heavy, flat sadness' in their chest.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient states that their sadness makes everything they used to care about feel 'completely useless.'
symptom_reasoning.S029: The patient notes that their arms and legs feel heavy and refers to being 'physically exhausted.'
symptom_reasoning.S083: The patient expresses despair about the future, stating there is 'absolutely no point' in trying to build the life they had planned and asking 'why bother?'

turns.doctor_question: Looking back at your life, even during your teenage years or early adulthood, have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt this same level of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?
turns.patient_response:
Um, looking back... honestly, no. Not like this. I mean, obviously, when I was a teenager in high school, I had days where I was moody or didn't want to do my homework, but it was never, ever this total loss of... of just who I am. Because this feeling, it's been going on for way longer than two weeks now, and it's completely changed my entire personality. 

Like, when the doctor asks about losing interest in things... it's just so extreme for me right now. I used to be such an outgoing person. At the salon, I was the one who would just chat for hours with my clients. We'd talk about everything—their kids, their vacations, whatever reality TV shows we were all watching. I loved making those connections. And I was always the first one to jump in and help the newer stylists, too. If one of the recent grads was struggling with a tricky foil placement or getting a toner mixed right, I'd be right there showing them how to do it. I really liked being that person, you know? The dependable one. And even outside of work, I was always doing things. My friends and I would go hiking up these beautiful trails just outside the city pretty much every other weekend. We'd pack lunches, take a bunch of photos for Instagram, and just spend the whole day out in the sun. 

But now... I don't do any of that. I really, really don't. It's like someone just flipped a switch and drained all the life out of me. Now, when I'm at work, I mostly just keep my head down. I barely say a word to the person in my chair, which I know is terrible for building a clientele, but I just can't bring myself to make the small talk anymore. I actively avoid the breakroom so I don't have to talk to the other girls, and when my friends text me to go hiking or even just to grab a quick coffee, I just leave them on read or make up some excuse about picking up an extra shift. I just avoid people completely. I just don’t have that spark in me anymore. It's totally gone. And it's so frustrating because I know I *should* want to do those things, I know I used to love them, but there's just nothing there now. Just this big, heavy blankness where my personality used to be, and I just want to hide from everyone because pretending to care takes too much energy.

symptom_reasoning.S023: The patient describes a profound loss of motivation, social interest, and emotional expression, noting a 'heavy blankness' and that their 'spark' is totally gone.
symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient describes a persistent 'heavy blankness' and feeling like all the life has been drained out of them, indicating emptiness and depressed mood.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly states they have lost interest in activities they used to love, such as hiking and chatting with clients, and no longer engage in them.
symptom_reasoning.S075: The patient reports actively avoiding coworkers, leaving friends' texts on read, and wanting to hide from everyone, indicating social isolation and detachment.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your weight since this low mood started?
turns.patient_response:
Um, yeah... actually, I have. It’s... it's kind of weird because I've always been a big foodie, you know? Like, the girls at the salon and I used to always do these big group orders for lunch, getting sushi or salads from that place down the street, or we'd swap recipes in the breakroom. But lately... I don't know. I’ve just been skipping meals without really meaning to. It's not like I'm on a diet or trying to lose weight or anything like that. I just... I completely forget to eat, or I just don't have the desire to even try. 

I'll get home at night, like around seven or eight after standing on my feet all day, and I'll just be sitting there on the couch in the dark and suddenly realize that the only thing I had the entire day was a coffee in the morning and maybe, like, a few bites of a granola bar I found in my apron pocket. And that's it. The thought of actually making dinner or even just scrolling through an app to order something just feels so overwhelmingly exhausting, so I just don't do it. I just go to sleep hungry, or not even hungry, just empty. 

And because I'm barely eating, I've definitely noticed my weight dropping. My clothes have gotten a lot looser. We have this strict all-black dress code at work, and I have these black trousers that I wear almost every day... they used to fit me perfectly, like they were tailored for me, but now they’re just bagging around my waist. I'm constantly having to pull them up while I'm trying to cut someone's hair, which is super distracting. I actually had to dig out this old belt I haven't worn in years just to keep them from sliding down while I'm working around the styling chair. So yeah, I guess I've lost a decent amount of weight, but it's really just because the whole process of eating just feels like way too much effort right now.

symptom_reasoning.S026: The patient confirms a significant decrease in appetite and unintentional weight loss, noting her clothes have become much looser.
symptom_reasoning.S029: The patient describes feeling 'overwhelmingly exhausting' at the thought of making dinner or ordering food, indicating a marked lack of energy.
symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient explicitly denies that her weight loss is intentional, stating she is not on a diet or trying to lose weight.

turns.doctor_question: Are you finding that you're having trouble falling asleep at night, or are you waking up much earlier than you intended to and finding it impossible to go back to sleep?
turns.patient_response:
Um, no, actually... it’s kind of the exact opposite for me. I don't have any trouble falling asleep at all. Because, like I was saying before, by the time I get home from the salon, I am just so completely wiped out. I’ll walk in the door, kick off my work shoes—which, by the way, are supposed to be these super expensive, ergonomic clogs that all the senior stylists recommended so your back doesn't hurt, but I'm just so heavy and exhausted that my legs throb anyway—and I just crash. I don't even turn on the TV or look at my phone or do my skincare routine to wind down like I used to. I just crawl under the covers, usually still in my black work clothes if I'm being completely honest, and I am out almost instantly. It’s like my body just completely shuts down because it just can't handle being awake anymore. 

And as for waking up early... no, definitely not. I never wake up earlier than I intend to. Honestly, it’s a massive struggle just to wake up when I'm *supposed* to. I have to set, like, five different alarms on my phone now just to make sure I don't miss my morning shift. I have them spaced out—6:00, 6:10, 6:15, 6:20—and I use that really obnoxious, blaring radar sound, just to try and force myself awake. But even with all of that going off right next to my head, I’ll just hit snooze over and over again. I just want to stay in bed forever. The thought of getting up and facing the day, putting on a full face of makeup, doing my own hair so I look presentable and trendy for my clients... it just feels so impossible. I just want to pull the heavy duvet back over my head and sleep through the whole day. So, yeah, falling asleep and staying asleep isn't the problem at all. I don't wake up in the middle of the night or anything. If anything, I just never want to wake up at all.

symptom_reasoning.S027: The patient denies insomnia but describes hypersomnia, stating it is a massive struggle to wake up and she wants to sleep through the whole day.
symptom_reasoning.S029: The patient describes being 'completely wiped out,' 'heavy and exhausted,' and says her body 'completely shuts down' from lack of energy.
